entities.summary:
Lucius Neratius Priscus (Unknown-Unknown) was a prominent Roman jurist and senator who played a crucial role in shaping the country's legal landscape. As the head of the Proculeian school, he significantly contributed to the development of Roman law. His tenure as suffect consul in 97 CE, alongside Marcus Annius Verus, marked a pivotal moment in Roman history.

    

    The legacy of Lucius Neratius Priscus can be seen in the continued influence of Roman law on modern legal systems. His work on the Twelve Tables, a foundational document of Roman law, remains widely studied and referenced today. Moreover, his appointment as a quaestor in 73 CE demonstrates the importance of his position within the Roman administration.

    

    The impact of Lucius Neratius Priscus's leadership can be seen in the subsequent Roman civil wars, which he navigated with relative ease. His ability to balance the interests of rival factions and maintain stability in the face of turmoil ultimately contributed to the Roman Empire's continued dominance. Notably, his involvement in the 96 CE succession crisis, which saw the rise of the 'Year of the Five Emperors,' underscores the complexity and intrigue of Roman politics.

    

    In conclusion, Lucius Neratius Priscus's remarkable career serves as a testament to the enduring power of Roman law and governance. His strategic leadership and legal acumen allowed him to navigate the treacherous waters of Roman politics, leaving a lasting legacy that continues to shape our understanding of the ancient world.
